# Currency Arbitrage Detection

## Problem

## Requirements

- Implement `has_arbitrage(rates: list[list[float]]) -> bool`.
- Input consists of an $$n \times n$$ matrix in which `rates[i][j]` gives the number of units of currency `j` obtained by converting 1 unit of currency `i`. Every diagonal value is 1.
- Completing an exchange loop charges a fee equal to 0.01% of the amount originally placed into the loop.
- Decide whether there is an **arbitrage opportunity**: an exchange path that begins and finishes in the same currency and leaves you with an amount strictly greater than the starting amount once the fee has been deducted.
- Return `True` when such an opportunity is present; otherwise return `False`.

## Examples

- `n = 2`, rates `[[1, 0.25], [4.0, 1]]` → `False`.

  The two conversions multiply the starting amount by $$0.25 \times 4.0 = 1$$, and applying the 0.01% fee makes the final amount smaller than what you began with.

## Hints

<details>
<summary>Hint 1</summary>

Convert the multiplication of exchange rates into addition by using logarithms, turning the problem into detecting a negative cycle.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 2</summary>

Use the Bellman-Ford algorithm to find negative cycles in a graph where edge weights are -log(rates[i][j]).

</details>

<details>
<summary>Hint 3</summary>

The fee of 0.01% can be incorporated by adjusting the rates or adding a small constant to the log-transformed weights.

</details>
